# Correction: the new components are Go, not bash

The repo owner has ruled: this redesign is the graduation point for the converge machinery.
Everything NEW you were briefed to build — status authoring, renderer, watch stream — is one
small Go program, not shell. The overall design from the original brief stands unchanged; only
the implementation medium of the new parts changes. If you already wrote bash for them, discard
it; keep your reading and any nix wiring that still applies.

## The tool

One Go binary, `converge-status`, living in cosmo (pick a sensible spot for a Go package in
this flake, e.g. `pkgs/converge-status/` with `buildGoModule`; follow whatever Go layout the
repo already uses, or standard cmd/ layout if none). Three subcommands:

- `converge-status set phase=building target=<rev> ...` — author a transition: validate the
  phase and keys, write the status file atomically (tmp+mv). Called by the converge unit script
  and its ExecStopPost line. This makes the binary the single owner of the schema; nothing else
  ever writes the file.
- `converge-status render` — read the status file + `/var/lib/reboot-pending/{state,last-blocked}`,
  emit one waybar JSON line. All precedence logic (building > failed > reboot-overdue >
  reboot-pending > current; stale = status file ancient/absent) and age formatting lives here.
- `converge-status watch` — render once, then fsnotify on the two state directories, re-render
  one line per relevant event, plus a periodic re-render (~5min) so tooltip ages stay honest.
  Runs on classic-laddie, invoked over ssh by the workstation side.

State-dir paths and the reboot-overdue threshold come from flags with production defaults, so
tests point the binary at temp dirs — same philosophy as the env-overridable roots in
`auto-reboot-scripts.nix`.

## Dependencies and style

- fsnotify is the one permitted third-party dep. Nothing else — supply-chain minimalism is a
  first-order concern in this repo. Pin via go.mod/vendor as buildGoModule requires.
- Terse comments, high info-density. No package-doc essays; the design rationale stays in the
  nix modules' comments where it already lives.

## What stays shell (glue only)

- The converge unit script: shrinks to its existing loop with `converge-status set` calls at
  the transition points; still factored out of the host module for testability as briefed.
- ExecStopPost: one `converge-status set phase=failed ...` invocation guarded as briefed.
- The workstation waybar script: a minimal loop — ssh laddie `converge-status watch`; when ssh
  exits, emit one `unreachable` JSON line locally (keep the current widget's stderr-diagnostic
  harvesting for the tooltip) and reconnect with capped backoff. No logic beyond that loop;
  anything smarter belongs in the Go tool.
- `auto-reboot-scripts.nix` untouched except the boot-time activation fix from the original
  brief.

## Testing

- Go tests run the REAL built binary (or its cobra-less main via exec) against canned state
  dirs: schema round-trip (set → render), precedence table, failed-with-target≠deployed
  (the behind state), stale/absent file, watch emitting on a file move into a tempdir.
- Replace/adapt the bash test derivations (`waybar-converge-test.nix`) accordingly; keep
  `auto-reboot-test.nix` green. Integration over mocks: drive the binary, not stubbed funcs.

## Acceptance (unchanged from the original brief)

- `nix flake check` passes — PASTE the final output lines; claims without pasted output are
  treated as not done.
- `git diff --stat` against main in the report.
- Report the transition-authorship map: which line of which unit/script issues which
  `converge-status set`.
- Commit and push before long verification; never background a nix build and exit without
  committing.
